title: Assertion TTL regression in private control plane leading to dropped audit events and RBAC stale grants
creator: Aisha Varma
description: Customers (AcmeCorp, FinSoft) reported intermittent authorization failures and gaps in audit logs on private clusters. Root cause: a regression introduced in control-plane token assertion TTL handling (edge case when IdP sends inexact NotOnOrAfter) that caused assertion cache entries to be evicted prematurely and audit emission to be suppressed during rapid KMS envelope rotation. Resulting symptoms: RBAC grants remained stale for up to 10 minutes after assertion refresh, missing audit events for role-bind changes, and failed SSO logins when failover routing occurred. This ticket coordinates an urgent patch, backfill for missed audits, and a release to private clusters with a staged rollout and rollback plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private control plane with SAML IdP that omits millisecond precision and uses NotOnOrAfter boundary equal to current time. 2) Enable KMS envelope rotate interval=5m and simulate simultaneous key rotation. 3) Exercise short-lived SSO assertions across two pods behind control-plane HA router. 4) Observe: assertion cache eviction log lines, subsequent denied API calls, and missing audit events in control-plane audit stream (kubectl logs and audit-sink).
mitigation: Temporary mitigation: increase assertion grace-window in control plane config to +30s and disable automated KMS envelope rotation for affected clusters. Suggested customer communication: instruct affected accounts to pause KMS rotation and apply runtime config change. This reduces risk while patch is developed and tested.
fix_summary: Adjust assertion time parsing to accept missing millisecond precision and treat NotOnOrAfter equal-to-now as valid for an additional 45 seconds grace window. Ensure assertion cache eviction triggers audit flush before removal. Add guardrails during KMS envelope rotation so audit emission is not suppressed when keys are rotating. Unit tests + integration test harness added for SAML edge-time handling and KMS rotation interplay.
deploy_plan: 1) Merge PRs and build control-plane image with tag cp-fix-assertion-2026-03-14. 2) Deploy to staging clusters for 2 hours with heavy SSO+KMS rotation load tests. 3) Canary deploy to 5% of private clusters (region US-WEST) for 1 hour. 4) Gradually ramp to 100% over 90 minutes, monitoring audit event rates and RBAC success rates. 5) Post-deploy backfill (see backfill_plan).
rollback_plan: Rollback by reverting image tag to previous stable cp-2026-02-28 and re-enable previous KMS rotation cadence. Automated rollback if error rate > 1% for 5m or audit-event-drop metric increases by >20%.
backfill_plan: Run audit replayer job that pulls raw request traces and re-emits audit events into customers' audit sinks for the interval 2026-03-09T00:00Z to 2026-03-11T23:59Z. Customers will be notified with summary of records re-emitted and SHA hashes for verification. Backfill job stored results in s3://redwood-backfill/ENG-36277/ and will be throttled per-customer to avoid sink overload.
customer_communication: Draft sent to customer success and account teams. Initial outreach made to affected customers with mitigation steps and ETA for patch. Follow-up scheduled post-canary with confirmed times for backfill. CS contacts: jessica@acmecorp.com, ops@finsoft.example, compliance@nimbushealth.org.
monitoring_checks:
- increase in audit_event_emit_rate (should return to baseline)
- RBAC_evaluation_denied_rate (should drop to baseline)
- SSO_login_success_rate (should improve)
- control_plane_error_5xx
test_plan: Unit tests for time-parsing; integration tests in staging with simulated IdP notOnOrAfter edge cases; chaos test that rotates KMS envelopes during active SSO sessions; synthetic traffic validating audit sink delivery. Acceptance criteria: zero missing audit events in 30m staging run; RBAC denied rate <0.1% under load.
regression_cause: A refactor of the assertion cache input normalization (PR #3930) replaced tolerant time parsing with strict RFC check and removed an audit-flush hook that executed on eviction during KMS rotation. Combined with a KMS rotation optimization that temporarily disabled audit emission, this produced a race condition.
